passage: Ishita, I saw your face at the Diwali dinner when Aunty announced your cousin's marks and then asked what you'd got. I'm Pranav, your Mama, and I remember that hot, sinking feeling. At your age I was the one compared aloud to my elder brother, in front of half our relatives. I went red and stared at my plate. What I understood later was that my mother's pride and worry were leaking out of her, and I happened to be standing there. It was never about my worth. So talk to your mother privately, not at the party. Tell her it hurts to be measured out loud. Then show her your effort your own way. I'll be nearby if you'd like company.

qa.q: Who announced the cousin's marks at the Diwali dinner?
What did young Pranav feel when he was compared aloud to his brother?
qa.a: He felt ashamed, hot and sinking, going red and staring at his plate while being judged in front of relatives.

qa.q: What could Ishita do about being compared at family gatherings?
qa.a: Ishita can ask their mother privately to stop measuring them out loud, and show effort in their own way.

qa.q: How might Ishita's mother feel about the comparison at the dinner?
qa.a: Her pride and anxiety were probably driving it, so she may not realise how much it stings, which is why a private talk could help. 🤍
